page_title: The Production Readiness Checklist for AWS

summary.title: The Production Readiness Checklist for AWS
summary.one_liner: A Gruntwork checklist of production-grade AWS infrastructure practices, covering secrets, backups, access control, and high availability before going live.
keywords: auto scaling group elb health checks
takeaways: Production AWS deployments involve hundreds of steps, and common gaps include plaintext secrets, untested backups, and shared SSH keys.
Use IAM roles on EC2 instances and restrict access to the EC2 metadata endpoint.
Run instances in auto scaling groups with ELB health checks, across multiple AZs, in private subnets behind NACLs.
Actually test database restores rather than assuming backups work.
Gruntwork says its Infrastructure as Code Library can deploy most checklist items in about a day via its Reference Architecture.
summary.summary: The page is a marketing-leaning article introducing Gruntwork's Production-Grade Infrastructure Checklist for deploying apps on AWS. It poses pointed questions about common gaps such as unencrypted secrets, unverified database backups, shared EC2 KeyPairs, EC2 metadata access, and ASG/multi-AZ/private-subnet design. The full checklist itself is linked rather than reproduced in the page text, which mainly covers its scope (server-side and client-side apps, CI/CD, architecture, security, monitoring). The page does not provide the detailed checklist items inline.
